hypothesis: Accumulating acceleration contributions directly cancels the target-mass multiply in each interaction against the final force-to-acceleration division, reducing arithmetic while preserving the source traversal and standard sqrtf-based distance calculation. The prior rsqrt-oriented candidates failed the largest-size correctness check, so this candidate leaves the distance calculation unchanged; changed rounding still requires controller validation.
notes: The supplied baseline is correct and has a three-repeat mean of 0.0018526411283622502 seconds. Both prior T4 arithmetic candidates failed one correctness check at n=16384 (maximum absolute errors around 0.00031); this proposal has not been measured. The supplied single_large_mass case uses n=1 and therefore does not exercise interaction scaling. The controller should validate all tolerances, nonfinite outputs, and extreme-mass behavior before timing.
transformations: Kept src/launch.json unchanged and retained one thread per target, the serial source traversal, float32 softening, and self-pair skip.
Changed each interaction factor to use source mass only, accumulating acceleration directly and eliminating the final division by target mass.
Retained the sqrtf distance calculation and velocity-then-position update order; the Particle copy still preserves mass unchanged.
